summary: Phantom codes are quantum error-correcting codes that implement logical entangling gates between all logical qubits purely through physical qubit permutations during compilation, achieving perfect fidelity with zero spatial and temporal overhead. Through exhaustive enumeration of $2.71 	imes 10^{10}$ CSS codes up to $n=14$, SAT-based search, and analytic constructions using quantum Reed–Muller codes and binarized qudit codes, the work expands the phantom-code landscape from two known instances to over 100,000 codes, and demonstrates one-to-two order-of-magnitude reductions in logical infidelity for GHZ-state preparation and Trotterized many-body simulation compared to surface codes at comparable qubit overhead.
motivation: Logical entangling gates account for substantial error budgets in fault-tolerant quantum computers, but conventional implementations require repeated measurement rounds, dense two-qubit gate layers, or ancillary codeblocks. Realizing this potential by jointly optimizing storage and computation requires identifying codes that support efficient logical gates with minimal overhead.
method: The authors systematically identify phantom codes via exhaustive enumeration with optimized Tanner graph canonical forms, SAT-based code discovery with Boolean constraint formulations, and analytic constructions from quantum Reed–Muller codes ($\lfloor 2^m, m-l+1, \min(2^{m-l}, 2^l) \rfloor$) and binarized $\mathrm{GF}(4)$ cyclic codes. End-to-end noisy simulations with Steane-style syndrome extraction, preselection-based state preparation, and spatiotemporal sliding-window decoders benchmark the $\lfloor 64, 4, 8 \rfloor$ phantom code against optimized surface codes under neutral-atom-calibrated noise ($p \sim 10^{-3}$).
result: For GHZ-state preparation on 64 logical qubits with 24% preselection acceptance, the phantom code achieves $\sim 56 \times$ lower logical infidelity than comparable surface codes; for eight-body Trotterized simulation, $\sim 94 \times$ reduction persists as system size scales, with advantages maintained at both near-term and projected future error rates.
